title: Degradation Impact Matrix and Operator Playbook for Tiered Model Fallbacks
author: Maya Liu
content:
Summary:

This page defines a compact: (1) Degradation Impact Matrix that maps observable signals to customer-facing impact tiers; (2) an operator playbook for executing tiered model fallbacks (model variant swap, regional failover, capacity tier demotion); (3) dashboard and alert configurations used during triage; and (4) retrospective triggers and roadmap actions. The goal is to reduce time-to-stable-state for multi-tenant LLM inference incidents while preserving unit economics and minimizing false-positive fallbacks.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted + dedicated inference traffic routed through the routing service (route-gateway).
- Covers model-variant fallback, autoscaler demotion, regional re-route, and temporary quota-based shedding.
- Not a replacement for full incident postmortem; it is an operator-facing stabilization playbook.

Audience:
- Platform operators, oncall SREs, runtime engineers, and platform product owners.

Key definitions:
- Impact Tier A (Critical): Customer-visible 5xxs or >20% tail latency violations for high-priority tenants for >5m.
- Impact Tier B (High): Token delay spikes where P95 > 2x baseline for a cohort or sustained token cost >10% of normal for >10m.
- Impact Tier C (Medium): Intermittent inference quality regressions (confidence drift), or modest latency increases for non-critical tenants.

Degradation Impact Matrix (observables -> actions):

| Observable                                   | Signal threshold                                    | Suggested immediate action            | Impact Tier |
|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-------------|
| 5xx rate (route-gateway)                     | >1% sustained over 5m for a tenant group             | Trigger model-variant swap -> Canary  | A           |
| Token tail latency (P99)                      | >2.5s absolute OR >3x baseline over 3m               | Promote warmset / regional reroute    | A           |
| Token cost-per-request spike                 | >20% above rolling 24h mean for >10m                | Apply soft quota / shed low-priority  | B           |
| KV cache miss ratio (model-serving)          | >40% miss rate for hot prefixes                     | Invalidate and force-prefetch         | B           |
| Embedding quality drop (eval monitors)       | Regression >5% on key prompt-set                     | Roll back quantization or swap model  | C           |
| Compaction/oom on worker                     | OOM alerts on >3 workers in a pool                  | Evict preemptible tenants, restart    | A           |

Alert and dashboard mapping:
- Alert name: route-gateway:5xx-spike - Severity: P0 - Page on-call. Trigger: 5xx > 1% for 5 minutes aggregated across route. Dashboard panels: "Route 5xx heatmap", "Tenant 5xx delta".
- Alert name: runtime:token-p99-degradation - Severity: P1 - SlackOps + Pager if for priority tenants. Trigger: P99 > 2.5s AND P95 increased >50% baseline. Panels: "Tail latency rollup", "Worker hotset occupancy".
- Alert name: cost:token-surge - Severity: P2 - SlackOps. Trigger: 24h rolling cost per token > 20% change. Panels: "Chargeback by tenant", "Token churn by model".

Dashboard panels (recommended fields and queries):
1) Route 5xx heatmap (Timeseries)
   - Metrics: route.gateway.http5xx.count by route, tenant.
   - Query example (PromQL): sum by(route, tenant) (increase(route_gateway_http5xx_total[5m])) / sum by(route, tenant) (increase(route_gateway_requests_total[5m]))
2) Tail latency rollup (Histogram)
   - Metrics: runtime.inference_latency_ms_bucket, report P50/P95/P99 per model variant.
3) Worker hotset occupancy
   - Metrics: runtime.kv_hotset_ratio{worker_pool} and runtime.kv_miss_count.
4) Cost-by-tenant sparkline
   - Derived: tokens_consumed * model_cost_rate.

Operator decision tree (short form):
1. Confirm signal: check primary dashboards and raw logs for 1x and 5x windows.
2. Identify scope: single-tenant vs cohort vs global. Use tenant-lookup and request-sample pipeline.
3. If 5xx spike (Tier A):
   a. Immediately route new requests for affected tenant(s) to the canary variant of the same model (model-variant swap).
   b. If canary reduces 5xxs within 3m, roll traffic by 25% steps to full promotion.
   c. If canary fails, promote regional fallback (route to compatible older model variant in alternate region).
4. If tail latency (Tier A/B): check warmset occupancy: if warmset<70% for the hotset, trigger warmset pre-warm job and promote warm instances.
5. If token-cost surge (Tier B): enable temporary soft quota and go to graceful degradation mode for non-critical tenants; notify Growth/Sales for potential customer impacts.
6. If quality regression (Tier C): roll back quantization profile or swap to the previous verified model revision and kick an eval job against the canonical prompt-set.

Operator runbook checklist (step-by-step):
1) Triage (0-5m)
   - Open the incident channel and link dashboards.
   - Run automated scope detection script: sh tools/scope-detect.sh --window=10m --route=$ROUTE (outputs tenant list).
   - Collect three representative request traces (trace IDs).
2) Stabilize (5-20m)
   - Execute model-variant swap: POST /operator/api/v1/swap-variant {"tenant": "<T>", "from": "v2-quant", "to":"v1-fp16-canary", "percent": 100, "reason":"auto-5xx-swap"} (sample CLI: rdoctl runtime swap-variant --tenant <T> --from v2-quant --to v1-fp16-canary --force)
   - For warmset shortfalls: rdoctl worker preheat --pool <pool> --prefix <prefix> --count 10
   - For capacity OOMs: evict preemptible: rdoctl pool evict --pool <pool> --policy preemptible-first
3) Monitor (20-60m)
   - Watch P95/P99 windows and 5xxs; if stable for 15m, begin rollback of temporary quotas.
   - If loss of stability or cascading failures, escalate to SRE lead and start regional failover checklist.
4) Recover and communicate (60-180m)
   - If root-cause is model/quantization, create a rollback CR and schedule a controlled rollout.
   - Notify affected customers via CS template: "We investigated a transient degradation and applied a temporary model fallback. We will follow up with a postmortem."

Quick commands cheat sheet:
- Swap variant (canary): rdoctl runtime swap-variant --tenant <T> --from <old> --to <new> --percent 100
- Force prewarm: rdoctl worker preheat --pool <pool> --prefix <prefix> --count 5
- Derate non-critical tenants: rdoctl quota set --tenant <T> --tokens-per-minute <n> --mode soft
- Query tenant 5xx in last 5m (Influx/Prometheus): rdo_query "sum(increase(route_gateway_http5xx_total{tenant=\"$T\"}[5m]))"

Configuration table (operational knobs):

| Config key                          | Default        | Allowed range        | Responsible owner |
|-------------------------------------|----------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| route.fallback.canary.window_mins   | 3              | 1-10                 | runtime-ops       |
| runtime.warmset.target_percent      | 85%            | 60%-95%              | serving-runtime   |
| quota.soft-shedding.threshold_pct   | 110%           | 100%-200%            | eng-platform      |
| model.variant.promotion_step_pct    | 25%            | 10%-50%              | model-onboarding  |
| prewarm.batch_size                  | 10             | 1-50                 | runtime-ops       |

Retrospective triggers and template:
- Trigger a retrospective if any of the following are true:
  - Rollout invoked emergency rollback OR model-variant swap reversed more than once within 24h.
  - Customer-impacting Tier A incident with >30m impact window.
  - Any automation action (auto-swap or auto-shed) caused downstream failures.

Post-incident template (use in retrospective):
1) Summary: short incident narrative.
2) Timeline: minute-level events (include alert timestamps).
3) Impact: tenants affected, duration, and SLO burn.
4) Root cause analysis: technical cause(s) and contributing conditions.
5) Corrective actions: short-term mitigations, owner, due date.
6) Preventative work: roadmap items and owners.

Roadmap (next 6 quarters) - prioritized items:
- Q1 (next quarter): "Fallback decision laboratory" - build a simulator to run candidate fallback policies against replayed traffic (owner: eng-platform, target: 2026-04-30).
- Q2: Automated warmset orchestration integration + safety checks (owner: serving-runtime).
- Q3: SLO-aware model variant scheduler (mix cost/latency) with operator UI (owner: runtime-ops + product).
- Q4: Customer-facing incident transparency feature (partial tenant status page + throttling explanations) (owner: customer-success + eng-platform).

Retrospective and metrics to track post-rollout:
- Mean time to stabilization (MTTS) for Tier A incidents. Target: < 25 minutes after playbook enacted.
- False-positive fallback rate. Target: < 3% of fallbacks per month.
- Percentage of fallbacks that resolved without rollback. Target: > 80%.

Ownership and contact matrix:
- Primary operator: runtime-ops-oncall (pager rotation).
- Secondary: eng-platform-shift (Slack channel #platform-ops).
- Escalation: SRE Lead (Owen McCarthy), Product owner (Rina Patel).

References and appendices:
- Example eval job to sanity-check quality after swap (can be run from CI):
  - jobs/evals/run_eval.sh --model v1-fp16-canary --prompts prompts/key_promptset.json --metrics precision,recall,bleu
- Sample incident channel template and customer communication snippets are in /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-briefing-card-library-and-incident-deck-templates-2026
